issues.description: Animal constructor signature conflicts between the problem statement/UML and the reference solution. The UML/problem statement defines Animal with attributes name:String and age:int and requires a constructor Animal(String, int). The solution implements Animal with only a name field and a constructor Animal(String), omitting age entirely. Students following the UML will implement/expect an age field and a two-argument constructor, which will not match the provided reference implementation and any tests derived from the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make all artifacts consistent. Either (a) update the solution to match the UML by adding `private int age;`, changing the constructor to `Animal(String name, int age)`, adding `getAge()/setAge()`, and updating Pig/Goat/Seal constructors accordingly; or (b) update the UML/problem statement to remove `age` and change the constructor to `Animal(String)`.

issues.description: Animal attributes conflict between the problem statement/UML and the reference solution. The UML/problem statement specifies Animal has both `name: String` and `age: int`, but the solution defines only `private String name` and has no `age` field at all. This inconsistency makes it unclear to students whether they must implement/store age and can cause structural test failures depending on which artifact tests are based on.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal fields with the intended specification: either add `age` to the solution (and corresponding accessors/constructor parameters), or remove `age` from the UML/problem statement so it matches the solution.
